A credit score (300‑900) shows how well you have repaid past loans and credit cards. The other checks – your monthly income of **₹40,000** and your employment tenure of **18 months** – met the required criteria. I can show you what would need to change for the loan to meet the checks, or answer any other questions you have.

unattributedPrompts: What does the lending policy say about the minimum credit score?

messages.name: odv2spoc41
messages.text: Why was my loan rejected?

messages.name: odvouk1qul
messages.text: Your loan was rejected because two checks did not meet the synthetic prototype policy thresholds: - **Existing EMIs vs income (FOIR)** – your fixed‑obligation‑to‑income ratio is **55.0%**, but it must be **at most 45.0%**. FOIR measures the part of your monthly income already going to loan EMIs and other fixed payments. - **Credit score** – your credit score is **640**, while the minimum required is **700**. A credit score (300‑900) shows how well you have repaid past loans and credit cards. The other checks – your monthly income of **₹40,000** and your time in the current job of **18 months** – met the required criteria. I can show you what would need to change for the loan to meet the checks, or answer any other questions you have.

messages.name: ogf6nqav37
messages.text: What if my credit score was 800, my monthly income was 90000, my monthly obligations were 5000 and my employment tenure was 60 months?

messages.name: ogftni8cqm
messages.text: - This is a simulation using the synthetic prototype policy (synthetic‑v1); your original application and its rejection remain unchanged. - With a credit score of **800** (required ≥ 700), the credit‑score check would be met. - With a monthly income of **₹90,000** (required ≥ ₹40,000), the income check would be met. - With monthly obligations of **₹5,000**, the FOIR (fixed‑obligation‑to‑income ratio) would be **5.6 %**, which is below the maximum 45 % and would meet that check. - With an employment tenure of **60 months** (required ≥ 18 months), the job‑tenure check would be met. Thus, under the synthetic prototype policy, the changed numbers would meet all four synthetic thresholds, but this is only a hypothetical scenario and not a new decision or guarantee.

messages.text: Your loan was rejected because two checks did not meet the synthetic prototype policy thresholds: - **Existing EMIs vs income (FOIR)** – your fixed‑obligation‑to‑income ratio is **55.0%**, but it must be **at most 45.0%**. FOIR measures the part of your monthly income already going to loan EMIs and other fixed payments. - **Credit score** – your credit score is **640**, while the minimum required is **700**. A credit score (300‑900) shows how well you have repaid past loans and credit cards. The other checks – your monthly income of **₹40,000** and your time in the current job of **18 months** – met the required criteria. I can show you exactly what would need to change for the loan to meet the checks, or answer any other questions you have.

messages.name: 56arefjjeo
messages.text: What if my credit score was 800, my monthly income was 90000, my monthly obligations were 5000 and my employment tenure was 60 months?

messages.text: - This is a simulation using the synthetic prototype policy (synthetic‑v1); your original application and its rejection remain unchanged. - With a credit score of **800** (required ≥ 700), the credit‑score check would be met. - With a monthly income of **₹90,000** (required ≥ ₹40,000), the income check would be met. - With monthly obligations of **₹5,000**, the FOIR (fixed‑obligation‑to‑income ratio) would be **5.6 %**, which is below the maximum 45 % and would meet that check. - With an employment tenure of **60 months** (required ≥ 18 months), the job‑tenure check would be met. Thus, under the synthetic prototype policy, the changed numbers would meet all four synthetic thresholds, but this is only a hypothetical scenario and not a new decision or guarantee.

messages.text: Bajaj Finance states that a CIBIL (credit) score of 650 or higher is required for a personal loan; scores below 650 do not meet the minimum eligibility.
